clips.linkedin:
Hand AI your product range and the buyer's guides AI cites, and it tells you where you're missing.

In our indoor cycling study, Google's AI Overviews cited YouTube in 65% of the overviews we saw. ChatGPT cited it twice in 780 answers. Claude and Perplexity never did.

So the place your reviews live affects which engines cite them. Video matters for Google. Written buyer's guides do the work everywhere else.

The job to give AI is a guide audit. Give it the list of guides the engines cite for your category plus your current range with prices, and it hands back a table showing whether you're in each one and what's out of date.

The podcast voices are AI-generated. Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/which-websites-does-ai-cite-indoor-cycling/
clips.text: In the first study, video and forum sites were only three to five per cent of citations. But that average hides a split. Google's AI Overviews cited YouTube in sixty-five per cent of the overviews we saw. ChatGPT cited it twice in seven hundred and eighty answers. Claude and Perplexity, never. So if Google is the engine you care about, honest video reviews of your product matter. If it's Claude or Perplexity, the written guides do the work.

Hand AI your product range and the buyer's guides AI cites, and it tells you where you're missing.

Our study of UK indoor cycling questions found a few buyer's guides carry most of what AI engines cite. BikeRadar's smart trainer guide was in 55% of trainer answers.

Two jobs to give AI. First, the guide audit. Give it the page list and your current range with prices, and it returns a table of each guide, whether you're in it and what's out of date. The pitch to the editor stays with a person.

Second, a comparison page drafted from your spec sheets and your rivals' public pages, fair to the rivals, with every claim checked before it goes up.

The podcast voices are AI-generated. Full episode, article and prompts at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/which-websites-does-ai-cite-indoor-cycling/
clips.text: Get AI on this. First, the guide audit. Make a list of the buyer's guides the engines cite for your category, and have AI check whether your current models and prices are in each one. Give it the page list from the report and your current range with prices. It hands back a table of each guide, whether you're in it, which model it shows, and what's out of date. The pitch to the editor stays with a person. Second, the comparison page. If you're going to publish one, have AI draft it from your own spec sheets and your rivals' public pages. And tell it to be fair to the rivals, because the page that got cited in this study compared real competitors. You check every claim before it goes up.
